licence: MIT (Almond's own models, generated by almond_mcp.structural_references)
purpose: Benchmarked building typologies as parametric line models. Each reference is built by code (almond_mcp.structural_references), converted to the same conditioned-model JSON the Rhino bridge exports, and analysed by validate_structure's native engine with its own benchmark loads. The same builders are cross-checked against OpenSees (benchmarks/) and closed forms (tests/test_structural_typologies.py), so a reference run shows what a correct Almond result looks like for that typology before a user's own geometry is checked.
conventions: Builders are SI (m, kN) and S355 steel with hollow sections, the sections the Rhino bridge exports.
Loads are the benchmark loads: case G (permanent) and Q (variable). Wind (case W) is dropped: Almond's checks are gravity combinations with a sway imperfection.

Planar (x-z) textbook models are made 3D by restraining y at the supports and giving every other node a lateral-y restraint (the deck or bracing a planar truss relies on); bars become hinged members. In-plane statics are unchanged.

Pin-jointed bars carry almond:release = bar (both axes released); planar truss members and simple beams carry hinged (major axis only, continuous in plan). The model protocol carries typed supports (almond:support grammar) or plain anchor points.
A reference's default study is the setting that reproduces the benchmark: material, self weight, support default, connections and the deflection span.

references.title: Rigid moment frame
references.summary: Multi-storey, multi-bay 3D moment frame on fixed bases: RHS columns and beams with rigid joints, beam line loads on every floor.
references.exercises: 3D rigid frame, beam UDLs (G 15 + Q 10 kN/m on x beams, 5 + 3 on y beams), sway buckling and the EN 1990 combinations.
references.supports: Fixed column bases (anchor points). fixed_supports=False pins them: the frame then relies on its rigid joints alone and alpha_cr drops.

verification.opensees: linear displacements, reactions and member forces to ~1e-9; alpha_cr within 1 %; P-Delta within 1 % (benchmarks/)
verification.invariance: rigid rotation and survey offset change nothing

teaching: Beam deflection is measured relative to the columns that carry it, so column shortening in the upper storeys does not count against L/250.
Watch alpha_cr in the stability report: below 10 the solver switches to second-order analysis on its own.
Try connections=simple: with pinned beam ends the unbraced frame needs its fixed bases to stand.

references.title: Braced tower
references.summary: Pinned-base tower with simple (pin-ended) beams and X-braced bars in the middle bay of every face; optional plan bracing stands in for a floor diaphragm.
references.exercises: Member end releases, truss bars, a tall model and the diaphragm question: without plan_bracing only the beams' weak axis ties the floors in plan.

parameters.name: plan_bracing
parameters.label: Plan bracing at the floor corners

references.supports: Pinned column bases (anchor points; the study default). The beams and braces carry their own almond:release = pinned, so connections stays rigid for the columns.

verification.opensees: linear to 1e-3 (OpenSees needs penalty links for the end releases); alpha_cr within 1 %
verification.note: The plan-bracing-off instability is correct behaviour, found by both solvers.

teaching: Without plan bracing alpha_cr is about 3.6 and the solver switches to second-order analysis; set plan_bracing=true and it roughly doubles. The benchmark's plan-bracing-off instability appears under the wind combination, which Almond does not run.
A pin-ended beam carries its UDL as a simply supported span: compare its L/delta with the moment frame's.
Braces are bars (released in both axes); the solver restrains the unstiffened rotations it finds and says so in the warnings.

references.title: Pratt truss
references.summary: Statically determinate planar Pratt truss on a pin and a roller, point loads on the top chord.
references.exercises: Pin-jointed bars, a determinate system (method of joints is exact) and a virtual-work deflection.
references.supports: Typed: pinned at one end, roller-x (slides along the span) at the other, lateral-y at every other node.

methods: method of joints: every member force to 1e-9

teaching: Every member is a bar: the checks are pure axial (tension, or compression with flexural buckling over the bar length).
Deflection is judged against the truss span (span_m follows the span parameter), not the panel length.
Halve the depth and watch chord forces and deflection grow; the method of joints predicts the forces exactly.

references.title: Pinned-base gable portal
references.summary: Single planar gable portal: two columns, two rafters, rigid eaves and apex, pinned bases, vertical load per metre of plan on the rafters.
references.exercises: A once-redundant frame: the horizontal thrust at the bases follows from the force method, the eaves and apex moments from statics.

parameters.name: w
parameters.label: Rafter load per metre of plan

references.supports: Typed: pinned at both bases, lateral-y at the eaves and apex (a planar frame on two pins alone can swing out of its plane in 3D).

methods: force method: base thrust and eaves moment to 0.5 %

teaching: Compare the base thrust with the force-method value in the checks: bending only there, bending plus axial strain here (well under 0.5 % apart).
At w=6 kN/m the 30 m portal deflects 151 mm (limit 120 mm); the default 4 kN/m passes. Set rise=0 for a flat portal.
fixed_supports has no effect here: the typed pinned supports describe the textbook frame.

references.title: Portal-frame warehouse
references.summary: A row of pitched portal frames on pinned bases, tied by pin-ended purlins, with X bracing in the two end bays; snow and roof dead load per m2 of plan.
references.exercises: A complete hall: rigid frames in one direction, bracing and purlins in the other, releases and bars together.
references.supports: Pinned column bases (anchor points; the study default).

verification.opensees: linear to 1e-3 (end releases via penalty links); alpha_cr within 1 %
verification.note: The benchmark idealises the bracing as axial-only bars (alpha_cr 3.0 at the 6-frame size). The reference model carries them as released beams, as the Rhino bridge would, so Almond also finds the Euler buckling of the slender CHS 88.9x5 roof diagonals (alpha_cr about 1.2): the X-bracing governs.

teaching: The roof X-bracing diagonals (CHS 88.9x5, about 8.5 m) fail the EN 1993 flexural buckling check as compression members long before the portals do. Real X-bracing is tension-only, which Almond does not model; read the result as 'size the braces or brace differently', not as a portal failure. The study runs first-order (stability=off) because with alpha_cr about 1.2 the second-order iteration takes minutes; pass stability='auto' to see it.
The end frames carry half the tributary width: see their lower utilization in detail=True.
Purlins are pin-ended in both axes; the bracing bars give the row its stiffness along the hall.
Raise q to find the snow load at which the rafters govern.

references.title: Double-layer space grid
references.summary: Square-on-square double-layer grid of bars (top chords, bottom chords and diagonals) pinned at edge columns every three modules, with area loads on the top nodes.
references.exercises: Many bars, a 3D truss and nodal G/Q loads; the dense solver's size limit as the grid grows.
references.supports: Pinned at the edge columns (anchor points; the study default). Edge nodes between columns are free.

verification.opensees: linear to ~1e-9 on the 12 x 12 grid (1,152 bars); alpha_cr within 1 %
verification.note: The benchmark uses nx=12; the catalogue default is 6 so the stability refinement stays small.

teaching: Bars in compression are refined for the buckling check (elements_per_member in the stability report); a 12-module grid is large for the dense solver.
Deflection is judged against the overall extent (truss types), the grid's span.
Compare depth 1.0 and 2.0: a deeper grid trades chord force for diagonal length.

references.title: Parabolic arch
references.summary: Planar parabolic arch as a polygon of n members, nodal loads w*dx at every interior node: the funicular load for the polygon.
references.exercises: Funicular statics (thrust = M0 / rise, no bending), in-plane buckling and second-order effects near the critical load.
references.supports: Typed from the ends parameter (pinned or fixed), lateral-y at every rib node.

methods: funicular statics: thrust to 0.1 % (rib shortening ~0.06 %), bending below 1e-3 M0
verification.opensees: in-plane alpha_cr within 1 %; near-buckling P-Delta amplification within 1 %

teaching: Under its funicular load the arch carries pure compression: the checks show bending below a thousandth of the equivalent beam moment.
Raise w: at 12 kN/m alpha_cr passes below 1 under ULS 6.10 and the verdict is an instability; at the default 5 kN/m alpha_cr is about 1.65 and the solver runs second-order (P-Delta) on its own.
Flatten the rise: thrust grows as 1/rise and the rib's utilization with it.

references.title: L-shaped cantilever
references.summary: Two horizontal CHS members at right angles, fixed at one end, a point load at the free tip: bending of both arms plus torsion of the first.
references.exercises: Bending and torsion together; the smallest reference, with a closed-form tip deflection.
references.supports: One fixed support (anchor point). fixed_supports=False would leave a mechanism: a cantilever needs its root moment.

methods: PL^3/3EI for each arm plus P b^2 a / GJ: tip deflection to 1e-9

teaching: The deflection limit is L/250 of the longest member (arm a), the frame rule; at the benchmark load P=10 kN the tip moves 123 mm, so the default study uses 0.8 kN. The closed form scales linearly with P.
Torsion is in the forces (T) but not in the EN 1993 checks listed as not covered: read the assumptions.
Lengthen arm b: torsion of arm a grows linearly, its tip contribution with b^2.

references.title: Cantilever canopy
references.summary: A row of fixed-base columns, each with a cantilever beam and a back-span, tied by an edge beam at the tips, with a corner point load.
references.exercises: Cantilevers with back-spans, an edge beam sharing an eccentric load, canopy deflection relative to the root.
teaching: As drawn the RHS 300x200x10 cantilever fails deflection (about 165 mm against L/250 of the 5 m arm): a sizing exercise, not a design. Deepen the beam or shorten the cantilever and run again.
The corner load is shared by the edge beam: compare the first and last cantilever in detail=True.
Deflection at a cantilever tip is measured relative to its root, so column bending does not count twice.
Lengthen the back-span to see how much it relieves the column moment.

references.title: Cylindrical diagrid tower
references.summary: A cylinder of inclined CHS diagonals with ring beams at every level on fixed bases; floor loads on the ring beams.
references.exercises: Inclined members only (local axes and orientation), ring beams, a tall tube: results must not change when the tower is rotated in plan.
references.supports: Fixed at every base node (anchor points).

verification.invariance: rotating the tower in plan changes nothing except the sway-imperfection direction (global x/y), a known 0.4 % effect

teaching: At the benchmark floor loads (25 + 12 kN/m on 5.2 m ring beams) the CHS 219.1x10 rings exceed capacity (utilization about 1.2): the reference fails honestly; the diagonals pass.
Every diagonal is a brace by orientation; the ring beams are the only horizontals, so the tube's stiffness is in the diagonals.
The sway imperfection acts in global x and y; a non-orthogonal plan is a known limit (research note 2026-10-20, finding 5).
Halve the number of segments: longer diagonals, lower alpha_cr.

references.title: Vierendeel girder
references.summary: Planar rigid-jointed girder without diagonals (two chords and verticals) on a pin and a roller, point loads on the top chord.
references.exercises: Shear carried by chord bending: a frame that looks like a truss but is not one.
references.supports: Typed: pinned at one end, roller-x at the other, lateral-y at every other node.
teaching: Compare with the Pratt truss: here the chords bend to carry shear, and utilization is governed by bending plus axial force.
Set connections=simple and the girder becomes a mechanism: the rigid joints are the structure.
Deflection is judged against the girder span (span_m follows the span parameter).

references.title: Frame on six support types
references.summary: Single-storey 2 x 1 bay frame whose six column bases are all different: fixed, semi-rigid (rotational springs), pinned, a roller sliding along x, a soil spring and a vertical-only roller.
references.exercises: Every support type of the almond:support grammar in one model, with their reactions.
references.supports: Typed, one of each: fixed; fixed rx=8000 ry=8000 (semi-rigid); pinned; roller-x; spring kx=100000 ky=100000 kz=50000 rx=20000 ry=20000 rz=20000; roller.
teaching: Read support_types and the per-support reactions (detail=True): a spring's reaction is its force on the structure.
Place it in Rhino to see the almond:support user text each point carries.
Replace the rollers by pins (edit the placed points' user text) and compare the reactions.
